solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Priest appearing in Yorkshire location as high-kicking presenter

indicators.note: the priest appears inside the place name, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Ripon is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A clergyman turns up in a Yorkshire town, cast as a television host famous for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Rippon, a BBC newsreader, famously showed her legs and high kicks dancing on the Morecambe and Wise Christmas show in 1976.
explanation.definitionFit: The newsreader Angela Rippon is remembered for her leg-kicking dance routine on a comedy show, so she is a high-kicking presenter.

clue.text: French writer among one admirer's possibilities

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the writer sits among the other letters, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: admirer's read as admirer is, i.e. FAN'S, giving FANS
George Sand was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A French author turns up among the options of a single devotee.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophes vanish in the grid: the phrase is "ifs and ans".
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for doubts and conditions lists hypothetical cases, i.e. what might be, so it means possibilities.

clue.text: Travel partners prepared capital application

parts.note: P&O, the ferry and cruise company, pairs the letters P and O
prepared means made, as in made ready

explanation.surface: Holiday companions draw up a request to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the head, not a city, so a capital application is something applied to the hair. P&O is a British ferry and cruise line.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented grease smoothed onto the hair, which grows on the head, the 'capital' of the body.

clue.text: Wanting balls, say, charging rising passion

indicators.note: charging is filling up, so one piece is loaded into the other
in a down clue rising means the word for passion is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a yen is a strong longing or passion
Ed Balls, the British Labour politician, is an example of an Ed

explanation.surface: Someone lacking balls as they charge at an increasing passion, a sporting rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' and 'charging' do the work. Ed Balls was Labour's Shadow Chancellor when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy and wanting both describe someone lacking what they require; a synonym in the adjective sense.

clue.text: Doctor admits target after projection

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the target goes inside the doctor's letters

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal, i.e. a target
on can mean after or following, as in later on

explanation.surface: A physician lets in an aim following some forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' looks like a forecast; here it is a branch sticking out from a nerve cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendron, or dendrite, is a branching outgrowth of a nerve cell, a projection in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Stopping row, my beloved's mustard!

indicators.note: stopping as in plugging a gap: the beloved fills the middle of the row

parts.note: a din is a noisy row
jo is a Scots word for sweetheart, as in Burns's 'John Anderson, my jo'

explanation.surface: Someone stops a quarrel to announce their sweetheart is a condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my beloved's' reads as 'my beloved is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dijon is a smooth French mustard named after the Burgundian city where it was made.

clue.text: Definitely not showing expertise in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word for expertise is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: know-how is practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses to display skill when giving a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect or informal adverb meaning in no way at all, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Potato cake, right? Big it up!

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for big

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word it is read upwards, i.e. backwards

explanation.surface: Someone praises a potato cake and urges you to talk it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a flat cake.

clue.text: October day? Pro, versatile artist, on London Pride

parts.note: in the Roman calendar the Nones of October fell on the 7th

indicators.note: versatile means able to turn many ways, so the letters of pro are rearranged

parts.note: William Etty was an English painter

explanation.surface: A date in October, a flexible professional and a painter take part in a London Pride event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'London Pride' suggests a parade, but it is a plant, a saxifrage.
explanation.definitionFit: The saxifrage called London pride has a folk name, none-so-pretty, praising its small pink flowers.

clue.text: Judge has united "unfashionable" stage performer and London wordsmith

indicators.note: has means holds, so the judge's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Samson was one of the judges of Israel in the Bible
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football team names

indicators.note: the quotation marks ask for 'fashion' to be taken away from the performer's name; ton is a word for fashion

parts.note: Elton John is a singer and showman on stage

explanation.surface: A judge with a flamboyant pop star, now dated, alongside a London man of words.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'unfashionable' means un-fashion-able: take TON, a word for fashion, away from the performer. 'Judge' looks like Samuel's role, but the judge is Samson.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Johnson compiled his great Dictionary of the English Language in London, so he is the city's best-known wordsmith.

clue.text: Line on unusual last dance ringed by extremely crapulent guests, we predict

definitions.note: the definition is spoken by the predictors themselves, so a plural noun stands for 'we predict'

indicators.note: ringed by means surrounded, so the extreme letters wrap round the rest
extremely picks the very ends of the phrase crapulent guests

parts.note: RY, short for railway, is a line

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of last are set in an unusual order

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: At the end of a wedding party, hungover guests circle the last dance and make forecasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes STAL from LAST. The definition is what fortune-tellers' glass globes would say if they spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortune-tellers gaze into glass spheres to foresee the future, so those globes speak as forecasters.

clue.text: Time to settle down West at last, and ready to reproduce?

indicators.note: to reproduce suggests making again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
at last picks the final letter of each of the words down and West

explanation.surface: A couple out West ready at last to settle down and start a family.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent day is the date when a tenant must pay what is owed, so it is a time to settle up.

clue.text: Special for good, we begin afresh

definitions.text: Special for good, we begin afresh

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the altered letters are put in a new order
Special for good means S takes the place of G

explanation.surface: A determined pledge to start again properly, for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping G for S turns WE BEGIN into WEBESIN, which 'afresh' rearranges; the whole clue is what beginners might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Newcomers to anything are starting over, so a group of novices could say they are starting from scratch.

clue.text: Show feelings in roadside motel

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Displaying emotion at a roadside motel, a honeymoon stop perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to express emotion openly, often theatrically.

clue.text: First passage of married life?

parts.note: the newlyweds' first walk together is back down the church gangway after the vows

explanation.definitionFit: After the ceremony bride and groom walk out through the gangway between the pews, their first passage as a married couple.

clue.text: Unwanted communication about page boy, little 9?

indicators.note: about means around, so the boy's name goes round the page

parts.note: 9 across is Samuel, whose short form is Sam

explanation.surface: An unwelcome message concerning the young pageboy at the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is junk email sent in bulk, communication nobody asked for.

clue.text: On film, he kept Clyde phosphorus-abundant, then -scarce

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus
abundant suggests high, and HI is a short form of high
scarce suggests low, and LO is a short form of low

explanation.surface: A film character's pet was fed a diet high, then low, in phosphorus.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphens make 'phosphorus-high' then 'phosphorus-low'. Philo Beddoe, played by Clint Eastwood, kept Clyde the orangutan in Every Which Way But Loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Philo Beddoe is the trucker in the 1978 film whose companion is an orangutan named Clyde.

clue.text: Nut, odd lecturer, shifted place name

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the altered letters appear in a strange order
shifted means moved out: the lecturer leaves and name comes in

explanation.surface: An eccentric academic has moved somewhere with a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks like slang for the odd lecturer; it is the definition. Replacing L in PLACE with N gives PNACE, which 'odd' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is an edible nut from a North American hickory tree.

clue.text: One unmentioned in hymn turning tide …

indicators.note: turning means the remaining letters are read backwards
unmentioned in means left out of, so one letter is removed from the hymn

parts.note: a paean is a hymn or song of praise
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: One person keeps quiet through a hymn as the tide turns.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing one A from PAEAN leaves PAEN, which 'turning' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap is a tide with the smallest range, occurring near the moon's first and third quarters.

clue.text: Behind one year, hirer heads off and out

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the remaining letters are rearranged
heads off means the first letter of each of the three words is removed

explanation.surface: A year late, the hirer's chiefs are gone and he is out of a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' leaves NE, EAR and IRER; 'out' rearranges them. The answer is a French phrase used in ballet and fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is used in ballet for a step moving backwards, so it means behind or to the rear.

clue.text: … and further extract from nuptial song

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Continuing the thought with a passage taken from a wedding song.
explanation.definitionFit: Also introduces an extra point, much as 'and further' or 'besides' does.

clue.text: Woman companion not against adoration

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

indicators.note: not here means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: love is adoration
V stands for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A woman's partner is all for worship, not opposed to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing V from LOVE leaves LOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloe is a woman's first name, known from Greek pastoral romance.

clue.text: Again wife rolled joint before this woman!

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: J is slang shorthand for a joint, a cannabis cigarette

indicators.note: rolled here means rolled off, so the letter for wife drops away

parts.note: anew means again

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a woman who has rolled another spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolled' removes W from ANEW, leaving ANE. The exclamation mark makes 'this woman!' point to a particular woman by name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane is a common woman's first name, standing for one particular woman.

clue.text: Escape sister, heading down when phone's ringing

indicators.note: ringing means encircling, so the phone's letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: TEL is short for telephone

indicators.note: heading down means the first letter is moved to the bottom, which in a down clue is the end

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

explanation.surface: A nun plots an escape while the phone is ringing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the 'heading' is the top letter, and 'down' sends it to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners escape by digging an underground passage, so a tunnel is a means of escape.

clue.text: Bust, daughter's slipping ring over end of finger support

indicators.note: slipping says a ring is slid into place on the finger, swapping one letter for another
over means placed on top of, so the ring takes the spot of the finger's last letter

parts.note: bust means broken

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of finger

parts.note: O is shaped like a ring
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: The daughter has broken things by slipping a ring over her fingertip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a noun but means broken; 'slipping ring over' swaps O, ring-shaped, for the fingertip letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookend is a support placed at the end of a row of books to keep them upright.

clue.text: Drink in bars betting money for old rope, loosely

indicators.note: bars means excludes, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: to soak up is to drink in or absorb
SP is the starting price in horse-race betting

explanation.surface: Drinking in pubs and betting cash in exchange for rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink in bars' suggests pub drinking, but 'bars' means excludes: SOAK UP without SP leaves OAKU.
explanation.definitionFit: Oakum is loose fibre picked from old tarred ropes, once used to caulk ships' seams.

clue.text: I announce bride, groom arrive finally outside establishment

indicators.note: outside means the final letters go round the establishment
finally picks the last letter of each of bride, groom and arrive

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A master of ceremonies announces the couple arriving at the venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters EME go round CE. The definition is the speaker's own words: a compère's job is to announce.
explanation.definitionFit: A compère or master of ceremonies introduces the acts, so one could say of the role 'I announce'.

clue.text: He is helping to get bridesmaids in edgeways — from below!

indicators.note: from below says the hidden letters are read backwards
helping to get says the clue words supply part of the answer's letters, a run inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man trying to lend a hand with the bridesmaids cannot get a word in edgeways.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'He is helping to get' as the definition; 'helping to get' is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is just 'He', a man's name. SINED inside 'bridesmaids in edgeways' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis is a man's given name, so it stands for 'he', some particular man.

clue.text: Discoloration making trouble strifeful?

indicators.note: strifeful means full of conflict, so the letters of trouble are in disorder

explanation.surface: A stain that causes conflict and trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-rot is a fungal stain that turns timber bluish, a discoloration of wood.

clue.text: Coloured fabric for outfit? Rating soars!

indicators.note: soars means rises; in a down clue the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothing, an outfit
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: A dyed fabric chosen for a costume sends its popularity soaring.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is cloth dyed in patterns with wax resist, a technique from Java.

clue.text: What's used to cut cake's not unusually consumed quite a bit of water

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the cutting tool holds the rest

parts.note: a lance is a blade used to cut, as a surgeon lances a boil

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of cake's not come in an unusual order

parts.note: the letters of cake's, its S included

explanation.surface: A knife to cut the wedding cake has not been used, but much water was consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's used to cut cake' suggests a knife; only 'What's used to cut' is the lance, and 'cake's' joins the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Constance, the Bodensee, is a large body of water bordered by Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

clue.text: Sue's rear pinched in Episode 1 of Mr & Mrs — happy days!

indicators.note: the end letter of Sue's name is pinched and tucked in further along
Episode 1 of picks only the first letter of Mr

explanation.surface: Sue is pinched on the bottom during the first episode of a quiz show for couples, those were the days.
explanation.walkthrough: SUE + M + MRS gives SUEMMRS; 'rear pinched in' moves the E later. Mr & Mrs was a British TV quiz for married couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Summers stands for carefree times, as in the 'summers of our youth', which are happy days.

clue.text: Passionate chap loses heart to overtures of luscious lady, stupendous!

indicators.note: the middle of the chap's word is lost and replaced by other letters

parts.note: a kisser is someone who kisses, a passionate chap

indicators.note: overtures are openings, so take the first letter of luscious and of lady

explanation.surface: An ardent man falls for the advances of a gorgeous woman: amazing!
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of KISSER is SS; LL, the opening letters of 'luscious lady', takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a 'killer' thing is excellent or amazing, as in a killer tune.
